newsitem.title: USA: Jammed door on shuttle puzzles U.S. space agency.
newsitem.headline: Jammed door on shuttle puzzles U.S. space agency.

text.p: NASA engineers scrambled on Saturday to find ways of fixing a stuck hatch on the space shuttle Columbia so two astronauts can leave the crew cabin for a space walk.
Officials at mission control in Houston met for two hours to discuss the jammed airlock hatch, which stopped a planned space walk by astronauts Tammy Jernigan and Tom Jones on Thursday night.
They planned to convene again at 3 p.m. EST (2000 GMT) to decide if a repair and space walk were possible on Saturday night.

The two astronauts were scheduled to test a variety of construction tools outside the orbiter. The tools will be needed to help build NASA's planned permanent space station. Construction of the orbiting outpost is scheduled to begin late in 1997.

"The around the clock analysis and testing so far has not identified a most like cause of the jammed hatch," said mission control commentator Kari Fluegel. "A decision to proceed with a space walk today will hinge on progress in the next few hours before the crew awakens."
The five astronauts aboard Columbia were due to start their 12th day in space at about 4 p.m. EST (2100 GMT). A repair and subsequent space walk could take place about five hours later.
Space agency officials want to be sure that if the hatch can be opened, the astronauts would be able to close it safely so they can return to the shuttle's cabin.

"We don't want to make matters any worse than they are at this point. We are not sure what the problem is," astronaut Jerry Ross at mission control told the crew before members went to bed on Saturday morning. The astronauts had stayed up late to discuss the problem with ground controllers.

The investigation was looking at a possible problem with the door's latching mechanism, which is located outside the cabin, or with the gear box which operates the latches. Engineers were also studying the possibility that the door had shifted in its frame.

"All the video surveys do not give us any visual evidence of anything that could have caused a jam," said Ross. "If it's in the gear box we believe there is nothing more we can do. There's a lot of people down here hustling as hard as they can, trying to get you guys out of the hatch.

Jernigan and Jones, wearing bulky space suits in the cramped airlock chamber, wrestled with the handle that opens the hatch for two hours on Thursday night before flight controllers cancelled the space walk.
It is the first time in the 15-year history of the shuttle programme that astronauts have encountered problems with the airlock hatch.
Columbia's astronauts were to make two space walks, aimed at practicing construction of NASA's international space station, the first part of which is due to be launched in November 1997.
The shuttle crew has deployed two satellites during its planned 16-day science mission and is not due back on earth until Thursday.
